title: F110 object-format choice on the existing setup flow
canonical_summary: Offer the object format on the existing Source Control setup flow when a repository is being created, show the discovered effective format when one already exists, disable any choice current capability evidence does not certify and say why, state that the format is permanent, and record nothing when setup is cancelled.
gui_classification_reason: The atom is a visible setup-flow control with disabled states, reason text, a discovered-format display and permanence copy.
negative_constraints: Do not offer a format that current capability evidence does not certify.
Do not show the engine default as a discovered format or hide an unknown behind a plausible value.
Do not record a chosen format from a cancelled or abandoned setup.
Do not restate the exact engine, command-line and repository-format qualification requirement.

title: F110 typed new-repository request extension
canonical_summary: Carry the chosen object format in one typed extension of the existing new-repository setup request, bound to the setup session and the exact Execution Host and Environment, with confirmation requiring acknowledged permanence and cancellation recording nothing. The format is never inferred from a display string, label, caption, abbreviated identifier or engine default, and no Jujutsu command is added.
gui_classification_reason: The atom defines the typed request extension and its identity and lifecycle rules; the visible control is a separate atom.
negative_constraints: Do not infer the object format from a display string, label, caption, abbreviated identifier or engine default.
Do not add a Jujutsu command, handler, event or request meaning, and do not grow the 31-command enum.
Do not confirm a choice without the acknowledged permanence copy.
Do not change a default object format or request cross-format migration through this record.

title: F110 owner-owned format evidence and certified profiles
canonical_summary: Hold object-format evidence in one owner record per format and exact host and environment, with four independent support states for engine, library, transport and provider. A format is selectable only when a current catalog certifies all four as supported with named evidence; otherwise it is disabled with a reason. Unknown is never promoted or demoted, and no engine version or universal SHA-256 support is certified.
gui_classification_reason: The atom defines owner evidence and certification semantics; the disabled control and its reason text belong to the setup-surface atom.
negative_constraints: Do not treat unknown capability evidence as supported or as unsupported.
Do not certify a format from a stale or unavailable capability catalog.
Do not restate format evidence on the setup surface instead of reading the owner profile.
Do not claim that SHA-256 is universally supported.
